source.title: Sharpness-Aware Training for Free
source.authors: Jia-Wei Du; Da-Quan Zhou; Jia-Shi Feng; Vincent Y. F. Tan; Joey Tianyi Zhou

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests a related sharpness–generalization relationship using the proposed trajectory-loss method and SAM’s sharpness measure, rather than the magnitude-aware measure in V7.
record.gate_note: Reports test accuracies for training methods and describes SAM-sharpness measurements. It does not report train–test gaps or test the listed claim versions’ specific conditions. Cited results for ESAM, GSAM, and LookSAM are not this study’s own experiments.
record.test_reason: The study uses the sharpness–generalization premise to develop SAF and MESA and reports their performance. It does not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison with norm and margin measures. SAM sharpness and test accuracy measure a related question. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors propose trajectory loss as a proxy for SAM sharpness, conclude that SAF obtains flat minima and strong CIFAR/ImageNet accuracy at approximately the base optimizer's speed, and present MESA as a memory-saving variant with additional computation. These are method-performance conclusions, not validation of V7's specific correlation.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces a trajectory-loss regularizer (SAF) or EMA-target variant (MESA); compares them with vanilla training and SAM. Uses standard image-classification training from scratch.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and architecture vary; reported accuracy differs across these settings. The authors state SAM sharpness is lower than SAF and MESA in the second half of training.

fits_no_version.finding: SAF and MESA improve test accuracy over vanilla training throughout Tables 1 and 3. They outperform SAM on ImageNet and on the larger CIFAR architectures, while trailing SAM on CIFAR ResNet-18 and ResNet-101.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trajectory-loss training improves image-classification accuracy over vanilla training in these tested settings, with its advantage over SAM depending on architecture and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 4b reports reduced SAM sharpness under SAF and MESA. SAM has lower sharpness during the second half of training, although SAF and MESA have better ImageNet test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lower unscaled SAM sharpness need not rank training methods by their ImageNet test accuracy; this does not test magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps.

record.problems: The study does not report training accuracy or train–test gaps, so test accuracy cannot establish a change in the gap. CIFAR comparisons are three runs with reported ± values; ImageNet table uncertainties are not stated. Some baseline results are reproduced, while ESAM, GSAM, and LookSAM values are cited from prior work.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported Table 1 or Table 3 classification-accuracy entries were left out. Figure 4a training-loss curves were not extracted because they do not report the training–test gap or a claim-version measure. Figures 2 and 5 are landscape visualizations without stated numeric results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error and resulting test-error trends.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparisons and tuning-dependent differences.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a large-batch penalty.
Dropout interventions, small-data effects, excessive dropout, and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.

Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus train–test gaps, similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm and margin measures. SAM sharpness and test accuracy do not establish these relationships.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equal-sized random removals and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1's blank cells caused extraction errors: ResNet-152 GSAM/SAF/MESA accuracies are 80.0/79.9/80.0%; LookSAM has no ResNet result. The omitted ResNet-152 MESA result is outside all versions, so it is not entered in missing. Figure 4a training-loss curves cannot supply training classification error or a train–test error gap. A fixed ImageNet batch size of 4096 alone does not test V5.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error across widths.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparison and large-batch generalization gap.
Dropout interventions and their interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with norm- or margin-based measures; does not report the train–test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
